correctness.rationale: The stated pointwise equivalence for arbitrary finite ell-infinity products is not established by the proof. Its indispensable converse assumes that a non-Delta unit vector x has a **norm-one norming functional** f(x)=1 with ||I-f⊗x||<2; that purported characterization is false. Exact counterexample from Abrahamsen–Haller–Lima–Pirk, Proposition2.3: in real l1 take smooth x=(1/2,1/4,1/8,...). Its unique norm-one norming f=(1,1,...) obeys ||I-f⊗x||=2 (test e_n with n→infinity), although x is NOT a Delta-point: the nonnorming g=2e_1* satisfies g(x)=1 and ||I-g⊗x||=1<2. The correct Lemma2.1 requires testing all functionals g with g(x)=1, not just norm-one f. This invalidates the asserted Delta-coordinate equivalence and hence the converse convex-hull separation step based on it; indeed the 2026 primary paper flags Delta points in ell-infinity sums whose coordinates need not be Delta. The useful forward direction from one Delta-generating factor is plausible, but the claimed full iff statement has no verified replacement proof in the assigned package. This is a motivated, documented correctness gap; NOT a numerical timeout and NOT a claim that the final iff has been disproved as a standalone statement.
residual_risks: Final iff theorem not shown false; it is not proved by this package. A stronger characterization of Delta points could conceivably yield a different proof.
The false norming-functional lemma is decisively refuted by a smooth l1 example and independent operator-norm calculation.

Published related infinite c0 convex generation is not the finite ell-infinity criterion. These comparisons are novelty evidence only, not correctness certification.
